Which transport fits each feature?

Polling, long polling, SSE or WebSockets

Internet &amp; networking · 2/7

Four ways to get live data

  1. 1Polling: the client asks again on a timer
  2. 2Long polling: the server holds the request until an update
  3. 3SSE: one long HTTP response streams text from the server
  4. 4WebSockets: both sides send messages at any time

Internet &amp; networking · 3/7

What a persistent connection removes

Periodic polling

  • Message waits for the next poll
  • Empty checks still cost a request

SSE or WebSockets

  • Server sends when data is ready
  • Travel time is unchanged

Low latency here means no queuing delay.

Internet &amp; networking · 4/7

Internet &amp; networking · 7/7

How to decide

  1. 1Both sides send at any time: WebSockets
  2. 2Server sends text only: SSE
  3. 3Delay is fine and updates are many: poll
  4. 4No SSE support in the client: long polling

Deep dive: Notification feed

Feed: Server-Sent Events

  1. 1Server streams text/event-stream on one response
  2. 2Browser fires a DOM event per message
  3. 3On a drop, the browser reconnects and sends the last ID
  4. 4For an image, send a link; fetch it over HTTP

Deep dive: Stock ticker

Ticker: push or batch?

SSE

  • Each price arrives when ready
  • One long-lived connection

Periodic polling

  • One response holds many updates
  • Fewer requests, saves battery

At high rates, long polling sends the most requests.

Deep dive: Chat messages

Chat: WebSockets

  1. 1Messages go both ways on one connection
  2. 2Each frame adds only 2 to 14 bytes
  3. 3The app builds its own reconnects and state
  4. 4Long polling is the older fallback
